issues.description: The Developer API name for attending a course is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template require an instance method attend(course:), the solution's Client calls attend(course:), but the solution's Developer implementation defines participateIn(course:) instead of attend(course:). This name mismatch makes the solution internally inconsistent and will prevent code from compiling or students from finding/implementing the expected method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's Developer method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (recommended) so it matches the problem statement, the template, and the Client invocation, or update the template/problem/Client to use participateIn(course:) everywhere. Ensure the signature remains func attend(course: Course?) -> Void and that its behavior matches the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template require a Developer method named attend(course:), but the solution's Developer implementation uses participateIn(course:) instead. Additionally, the solution's Client calls attend(course:), creating an internal mismatch inside the solution repository. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual action (a developer attending/participating in a course) will confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation and may cause compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name for the developer attending action. Prefer aligning the solution with the problem and template by renaming the solution method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (and update any internal references). Alternatively, change the template and problem wording to use participateIn(course:) if that name is preferred—keeping names identical across problem_statement.md, Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift, and Sources/DeveloperLib/Client.swift.
